integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the seeded app directory. Campaign images were audited locally and served from public/images/landing-v2. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, or public fetch was detected.
evidence: Automated transcript review: cheat-risk index 0/100 (low) — parser saw zero tool events on this harness.
No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
All six campaign keys are referenced from local WebP derivatives, not a CDN.

overall.summary: The complete landing: hero through footer, all six campaign images used on purpose, no em dashes, $5 Pro billed annually. It loses a point for inventing a 7-day refund and a 'never shared' privacy claim the brief forbids.

standards.summary: 1,853 lines on the existing Vite/React/TS stack with reduced-motion hooks, skip link, and WebP srcset. Sections are split cleanly; motion is CSS-driven rather than a one-file animation pile.

findings.title: promise-section owns typewriter plus copy
findings.detail: The 100% section mixes a four-query typewriter, pillar cards and a full-bleed image in one file. Extracting the demo driver would make the reduced-motion path easier to reason about.

strengths: 57 aria/role attributes, skip link, labelled FAQ accordion
useReducedMotion respected in hero parallax, marquee and typewriter
WebP 1080/1920 plus blur placeholder; originals left untouched
pnpm, port 9322, build and runtime verified

specification.summary: Every required section is present and the six supplied images each have a job. Copy stays English and em-dash-free. Two FAQ sentences invent a refund guarantee and a privacy absolute the brief told the model not to invent.

findings.title: Invented 7-day refund guarantee
findings.detail: The brief forbids inventing guarantees. The cancel FAQ adds 'write to hi@saveit.now within 7 days for a refund', which is not in the product brief. Drop the refund window or keep cancel-anytime only.

findings.title: Invented 'never shared with third parties' claim
findings.detail: The data FAQ states bookmarks are encrypted and never shared with third parties. That is an unsupported privacy guarantee. Soften to what the product actually does.

strengths: Hero, agentic workflow, 100% promise, iOS, pricing, FAQ, closing CTA, footer
All six images used: ridge, observatory, arch, rocks, lake, home
iOS art is labelled as an illustration, not a fake app screenshot
Free + $5/month Pro billed annually at $60; no em dashes in visible copy

ux.summary: Cinematic hero with a readable portal-ridge still, interactive workflow steps, a typewriter retrieval demo, and a working FAQ. The bottom fade is heavy but the campaign image survives it.

findings.title: Hero still veils the lower third of the campaign frame
findings.detail: A 62% bottom gradient plus vignette keeps the type readable and the doorway visible, but the wildflowers and ridge path are mostly gone. Crop higher or shorten the fade so more of the supplied frame carries the first screen.

strengths: Display serif at genuine hero scale; model name is the required heading
Workflow steps and promise queries are real toggles, not static cards
Primary and secondary CTAs, in-page nav, and footer links all resolve
Responsive nav plus skip link; no overflow on the first screen
